source_review.notes: Reviewed the primary Bernstein-Goodman MVCC paper and Berenson isolation report; current PostgreSQL 18 pg_snapshot, transaction-status, system-column, and isolation documentation; MySQL 8.4 consistent-read, isolation, read-view, undo, and index documentation; and current SQL Server 17 XSN/active-snapshot/row-versioning documentation. All ten cited destinations were retrieved and retained locally. Product field meanings, acquisition timing, read modes, and lifecycle claims are version/configuration scoped.

evidence: Checked half-open S=(low,high,A), status, creator/deleter visibility, tuple visibility, command order, fixed/statement/transaction snapshot, read modes, and snapshot-pin definitions.
Checked tuple xmin/xmax terminology is kept distinct from snapshot low/high and from product-independent creator/deleter roles.
Checked transaction-ID numeric order, commit outcome, active-at-capture membership, current status, and wall clock are never conflated.
Checked update/delete and own-command rules preserve one logical state per key.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The teaching tuple predicate is explicitly smaller than complete PostgreSQL, InnoDB, or SQL Server visibility implementations.

evidence: Independently derived the snapshot's eligible committed set as {1,3,5}, plus reader X8's own prior work, without invoking the chapter predicate.
Recomputed old A deleted by visible X5, new A created by X5, C retained because X4 deletion is excluded, and F visible through self rule.
Recomputed B aborted, D created by X4 active-at-capture, and E created at high boundary X7 as invisible.
The independent run produced visible rows A=120,C=300,F=600; later X4 commit excluded; higher X5 included; own X8 included; independent_invariants=True.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The successful independent set-based result is retained at artifacts/reviews/DBE-047/independent-recomputation.txt; a prior malformed generated command failed before evidence creation and was replaced.

evidence: Re-derived the exhaustive disjoint partition <low, middle-active, middle-completed, and >=high.
Re-derived that committed status is necessary but active/future exclusion is fixed at capture, so later commit cannot alter S.
Re-derived tuple existence as visible creation AND NOT visible deletion and update continuity as matched predecessor invalidation/successor creation.
Re-derived snapshot-capture/commit-publication linearization: completed-and-published before capture or represented active/future, with no missing middle state.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The proof assumes exact active membership, retained outcome, atomic capture/publication, correct command/self rules, and stable logical version ordering.

evidence: Reviewed low-1, low, every middle active/nonactive ID, high-1, high, active-to-commit after capture, aborted below low, and status/capture publication races.

Reviewed insert, update old/new pair, delete, reinsert, key change, duplicates, own prior/current/later command, trigger/cascade, speculative insert, subtransaction/savepoint rollback, and Halloween-style reprocessing.
Reviewed statement/transaction/current/locking/exported/imported/historical snapshots, mixed reads, replica staleness, safe timestamps, DDL/catalog behavior, and session read-your-writes.
Reviewed secondary/index-only paths, all-visible summaries, cleanup/status truncation, freeze/wraparound, crash recovery, long pins, evidence races, and privacy.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Expected staleness and isolation anomalies are distinguished from tuple visibility defects.

evidence: The repository verifier matched exact seven-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status for the creator/deleter model.
The model checks exact snapshot representation, unique logical rows, aborted/future exclusion, active-at-capture deletion retention, and own future-ID write visibility.

Manual review checked atomic capture, immutable eligibility, outcome use, same-snapshot creator/deleter decisions, own command order, one state per key, index equivalence, and metadata/version retention.
Draft validation accepted exact front matter, sections, ten examples, five exercises/answers, local links, citations, and executable evidence before stopping only for review evidence.
invariant_checking.notes: The finite model omits command IDs, subtransactions, concurrency, indexes, locking reads, cleanup, wraparound, exported snapshots, replicas, and recovery.

evidence: Reviewed eligibility partition for exhaustiveness, mutual exclusion, status requirement, and fixed active membership.
Reviewed creator/deleter tuple rule and its four logical cases.
Reviewed one-logical-version and capture/publication proof obligations, including update continuity and crash recovery.
Reviewed exercise answers for truth table, missing production facts, independent harness, snapshot choice, and expected-versus-defect incident diagnosis.
proof_review.notes: No proof of vendor visibility code, distributed global snapshots, serializability, cleanup safety in a specific deployment, or crash-recovery implementation is claimed.

evidence: The low/high/active predicate is explicitly called a teaching abstraction resembling but not implementing pg_snapshot tuple visibility.
Product acquisition timing and mixed-read descriptions are scoped to current official documentation.
Visibility correctness is explicitly separated from freshness, serializability, authorization, and audit history.
Audited visible, committed, active, future, fixed, atomic, current, exact, unique, safe, portable, and always language for assumptions.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Current transaction status is never presented as a substitute for status and active membership at capture.

evidence: The standard-library snapshot/tuple model executed successfully through the repository verifier.
A separate eligible-set calculation independently reproduced all selected rows and decisive boundary facts.
All ten primary/official sources were retrieved and checked.

Production conclusions require engine/version/configuration, exact snapshot acquisition, transaction/command outcomes, tuple/version/index path, read mode, cleanup pin, replica/apply, recovery, and invariant evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live database schedule, system-column inspection, read view, XSN snapshot, locking/current read, export/import, cleanup, wraparound, replica, failover, or crash was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter replaces scalar timestamp intuition with an active-set snapshot cut, derives creator/deleter/self-command visibility, and connects it to index, cleanup, isolation, and distributed boundaries.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed current PostgreSQL pg_snapshot/system columns, InnoDB consistent versus locking reads, SQL Server XSN active exclusions, boundary tests, mixed-read incidents, long pins, evidence races, and cross-engine nonportability.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet, executable seven-version trace, partition/tuple proofs, ten distinct examples, and five exercises progress from boundary retrieval through model testing, architecture choice, and incident transfer.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. The chapter does not certify vendor tuple visibility, snapshot capture, transaction status, command/subtransaction handling, index paths, cleanup, exported/distributed snapshots, recovery, or a production configuration.
